beginner.content:
Deep Dive: Internals - How It Works

Actions are evaluated at request time.

  • jsp:include: becomes JspRuntimeLibrary.include(request, response, "page", out, true), a RequestDispatcher.include.
  • jsp:forward: becomes a RequestDispatcher.forward after clearing the buffer.
  • jsp:useBean: looks the id up with pageContext.getAttribute in the scope and creates it when missing.
  • setProperty and getProperty: call setters and getters using introspection.

Deep Dive: Syntax Options & Variants

Action list and options:

  • useBean: id, class or type, scope; body runs only when the bean is newly created.
  • setProperty: param, value, or property="*".
  • include: page, flush.
  • forward: page.
  • param: name and value for include and forward.
  • Others: jsp:plugin (obsolete), jsp:element, jsp:attribute, jsp:body, jsp:text.
codeExamples:
<jsp:useBean id="prefs" class="com.example.Prefs" scope="session">
    <jsp:setProperty name="prefs" property="theme" value="dark" />
</jsp:useBean>
<jsp:forward page="/WEB-INF/views/home.jsp">
    <jsp:param name="from" value="actions" />
</jsp:forward>

// OUTPUT:
// theme is set only the first time (when the bean is created); home.jsp gets from=actions

<jsp:include page="welcome.jsp">
    <jsp:param name="user" value="Ashish" />
</jsp:include>

<jsp:useBean id="product" class="com.example.Product" scope="request" />
<jsp:setProperty name="product" property="*" />

<jsp:forward page="/ControllerServlet">
    <jsp:param name="action" value="addProduct" />
</jsp:forward>
<jsp:include page="footer.jsp" flush="true" />

<jsp:useBean id="user" class="com.example.User" scope="request" />
<jsp:setProperty name="user" property="*" />

<jsp:forward page="/ControllerServlet">
    <jsp:param name="action" value="deleteProduct" />
</jsp:forward>
Tag failed to render content.
<jsp:include page="header.jsp" flush="true" />

expert.content:
Mid-Level Notes

  • jsp:include runs the target and inserts its output, so each is compiled separately; pass data with nested jsp:param.
  • jsp:useBean finds or creates a bean in a scope (page, request, session, application) using id and class.
  • setProperty can bind all matching request parameters with property="*"; the bean needs a public no-arg constructor and setters.

Senior Notes

  • Prefer EL and JSTL for reading beans; useBean is mostly legacy, and the controller should create the model.
  • forward rule: do not write output before a forward, because a committed response cannot be forwarded (IllegalStateException).
  • Cost: jsp:include performs a dispatch each time; for static, rarely changing fragments the include directive is cheaper.

Deep Dive: Common Mistakes & Fixes

Mistakes and fixes:

  • Bean without default constructor: InstantiationException; add one.
  • Property type mismatch: conversion errors on property="*"; validate in the controller.
  • Mass assignment risk: property="*" binds any matching parameter such as an admin flag.
  • Relative page paths in includes behave differently from forwards; use context-relative paths starting with a slash.
  • Forward after output: IllegalStateException.
  • Code after forward: still executes unless you return; keep forward last.

Deep Dive: Performance & Tuning

Performance:

  • jsp:include costs a dispatch and a separate servlet call each time, so avoid it in tight loops.
  • Cache expensive fragments in the application scope.
  • Forward is cheaper than redirect because it avoids an extra browser round trip.
  • Bean scope: use the narrowest scope; session beans consume server memory per user.
codeExamples:
<%-- avoid: 500 dynamic includes in one page --%>
<%-- better: a single JSTL loop in the page, or a tag file --%>

// OUTPUT: (varies)
// 500 jsp:include calls: noticeably slower than one loop that renders the rows directly

expert.content:
Deep Dive: Real-World Scenario

Scenario: a legacy form handler using actions, and its modern replacement.

  • Legacy: useBean plus setProperty binds a form to a bean.
  • Modern: a servlet validates and builds the bean, the JSP reads it with EL.
codeExamples:
<jsp:useBean id="form" class="com.example.SignupForm" scope="request" />
<jsp:setProperty name="form" property="email" />
<jsp:setProperty name="form" property="plan" />
<jsp:forward page="/WEB-INF/views/confirm.jsp" />

// OUTPUT: (POST email=a@b.com&plan=pro)
// confirm.jsp renders the form bean with email a@b.com and plan pro (HTTP 200)
